Evidence & scope

Included after actual author, separate source-verifier and adversarial AI source-content reviews of exact approved bindings. Scope means the complete relevant available source documentation/methods actually recorded, with explicit bounded/unread pages, version differences and unknown rights, payload, construction or operations retained. No experiment, settled upstream rights, or human peer review is implied.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

frontiercode · access terms: Cognition’s creator article keeps FrontierCode tasks private to limit contamination while offering evaluation to model creators. Mercor’s1.1 description permits fair internet use but assigns zero to runs flagged for opening solution-bearing sources.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

frontiercode · evaluates: FrontierCode combines unit tests, build/lint commands, reverse tests on the original broken code, adaptive test alignment, scope checks and LLM quality judgments. Its creator describes adversarial hack reports, four-solution rubric calibration, pod review and final researcher review.

candidate.third11.frontiercode.checks-and-review.v2

  • These are creator-reported benchmark construction controls, not new independent review receipts or measured false-positive improvements.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

frontiercode · evaluates: FrontierCode requires every blocker criterion to pass before awarding a weighted rubric score, otherwise assigning zero; its creator article averages five trials per reasoning effort and reports the best-performing effort.

candidate.third11.frontiercode.scoring.v2

  • A blocker pass rate and a weighted quality score are different metrics. Best-effort reporting is not a best-of-five success measure.
